turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Good morning, sir. Please have a seat. I will check your blood pressure before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Thank you. I hope this is not an inconvenient time.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Not at all. Sleeve up, please. Did you climb the stairs?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I took the lift. I had a small coffee with breakfast, about an hour ago.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four. Pulse seventy-six. Weight seventy-nine kilograms.
[SEG0006] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Your medicine list shows Crocin six hundred and fifty milligrams, as required.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, that is not right. I purchase only Crocin five hundred. I have never taken the six fifty.
[SEG0008] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I will mark that for the doctor. Room two, please.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come in. Sit down. What is the problem today?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, doctor. I have been having pain in the stomach, and my sleep has been rather poor as well.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Show me where.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Here, the upper part of the stomach.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has it been, and what does it feel like?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. It burns, just below the breastbone. It began the night of my cousin's wedding dinner and it has simply stayed.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Every day?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, daily. It is worse after meals, especially spicy food. The minty Digene tablets ease it a little. I take two after lunch and two after dinner.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not vomited at all.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Black stools, or any blood?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. The colour of the stools has been normal.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not think so. My trousers fit just as before.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the sleep.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I fall asleep, and then I wake at two or three and lie awake. When this started I truly cannot say. Some weeks, perhaps longer. I cannot put a date on it.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you sleepy in the daytime?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): A little tired in the afternoon, yes. I do still go to the office.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): What is your work?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I am an accounts manager at a textile firm in Coimbatore. The audit has made the days long, though I should not take your time with that.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you drink alcohol?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Only socially, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): How much, in actual terms?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, a bottle of wine most nights, perhaps. I ought to have said so straight away. I did not mean to be vague.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any spirits or beer?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No spirits and no beer. Red wine only.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Previous ulcer, or any stomach diagnosis?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No diagnosis was given to me. Um, about six months ago, at the company health check, they said my liver test, the SGPT, was borderline. They did not give me the number.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you had an endoscopy, or an ultrasound?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No, neither one. Nothing more was done.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking, apart from Digene?

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Crocin, when the pain is really troublesome. It is the five hundred milligram one, not the six fifty written outside. I have used it only two or three times in these three weeks.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure tablets? Any sugar tablets?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None. Digene is the only medicine I take on a regular basis.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please lie back. I am going to press on your abdomen.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. I hope my belt buckle is not in the way.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): The abdomen is soft. There is tenderness over the upper abdomen. No guarding. No jaundice visible.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): That upper spot is sore, yes. I apologise for pulling away.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): The readings outside are fine. I will not repeat the pressure or the pulse.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): This is most likely acid-related pain, a gastritis picture. I am not calling it an ulcer on today's visit.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I see. I had hoped it was a passing acidity, but three weeks feels rather long.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): A bottle of wine on most nights means I should check the liver. I am ordering liver blood tests today.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Kindly do. The word borderline from that health check has been at the back of my mind.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am also starting pantoprazole, forty milligrams, one tablet by mouth every morning, half an hour before breakfast, for two weeks.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Do you wish me to stop the Digene?
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Carry on with Digene after meals if the burning is still there.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): May I still take a Crocin on a bad evening?
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Only sparingly, and not on an empty stomach.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Try to cut the wine down. This is not a lecture. A smaller amount will be gentler on the stomach and the liver.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): I will make a sincere effort. My wife has been of the same view, though she is not with me today.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you vomit blood, or the stools become black, go to the emergency department the same day.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): I will do exactly that. I shall not sit on it.
[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): For sleep, avoid wine close to bedtime, and keep the phone out of the bed. Come back in two weeks and bring the blood reports.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): In two weeks. Shall I arrange it at the reception desk?
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Collect the laboratory form from them.
[SEG0066] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sir, here is the form for the liver blood tests, and your slip to return in two weeks. Pantoprazole can be collected at the pharmacy counter.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you kindly. I will take the tablets and proceed to the laboratory.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, and doctor, the parking outside was rather tight today. I nearly turned back.
[SEG0069] person_3 (DOCTOR): Glad you did not. We will see you in two weeks.
